surfaces.part: seat cushion (top arm of the L)

answer.evidence: At x=24 and x=35 the seat is a lighter band at rows 13-19 (L=99) that ends in a bright front-edge line at row 20 (L=119). Below it is a darker front face at rows 21-23 (L=57), then the outline at row 24. The backrest above is a vertical face at rows 5-12 (L=72) with a 2-row highlight rim at rows 3-4. The south-running arm repeats the pattern: seat rows 21-40, edge line at row 41, front face at rows 42-44. The silhouette is an L (width 46 at rows 2-24, then 14 at rows 26-45). The seat surface is seen from above, so the object reads as three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a purple L-shaped sofa with only 8 distinct colours, against 11-40 for the references. Its shading is shallow: roughly a light edge, a mid purple and a dark purple, with no per-cushion highlights or stitching. The 48% flat-fill coverage means large cushion areas are one flat colour with no grain or dots, while the references sit at 0-13%. All of its dark edge pixels are neutral (100%), so the outline is a uniform near-black line around the shape, the 'sticker' look, unlike the tinted dark-material outlines of the hedge, stall and well. Its median of 6 colours per tile is far below the hedge (10), stall (17) and well (20). Overall it is flatter and thinner than the references.
